title: Testing & Observability in Next.js: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before notes on testing a Next.js app (Jest/Vitest, React Testing Library, Server Components and Actions, Playwright) and watching it in production (instrumentation.ts, error boundaries, error reporting, Web Vitals).

chapters.title: Testing Layers and the Mental Model
points: Testing pyramid for Next.js: many fast unit tests (Vitest/Jest + RTL), a few integration tests, a thin layer of Playwright E2E for critical user flows
Jest vs Vitest: Vitest is Vite-native, ESM-first, and has a Jest-compatible API (describe/it/expect, vi.fn instead of jest.fn); Jest uses next/jest with SWC transform
Async Server Components cannot be rendered by Jest/Vitest + RTL, so cover them with E2E tests (or test the extracted pure logic as unit tests)
Test behavior the user sees (roles, text), not implementation details (state, class names, internal calls)
Mocking boundary rule: mock network, DB and next/navigation; do not mock the component under test

chapters.title: Unit Tests with Jest or Vitest and RTL
points: Setup Jest: npm i -D jest jest-environment-jsdom @testing-library/react @testing-library/jest-dom; jest.config.ts uses createJestConfig from next/jest with testEnvironment 'jsdom'
Setup Vitest: npm i -D vitest @vitejs/plugin-react jsdom @testing-library/react; vitest.config.mts with plugins [react()] and test.environment 'jsdom'
Pattern: render(<Comp />), query with screen.getByRole('button', {name: /save/i}), assert with expect(...).toBeInTheDocument() from jest-dom
Interactions: use userEvent.setup() and await user.click(...) rather than fireEvent; use findBy* or waitFor for async UI
Run: npm test, vitest run (CI, single pass), vitest (watch); add 'test' script to package.json

chapters.title: Testing Server Components and Server Actions
points: Sync Server Components render fine in unit tests; async ones do not, so use Playwright for those
Test an async Server Component's data logic by extracting the fetch/query into a plain async function and unit testing it with mocked fetch
Server Action is just an async function marked 'use server': import it and call it directly with a FormData in a unit test
Mock next/headers, next/cache (revalidatePath) and next/navigation (redirect throws NEXT_REDIRECT) via vi.mock/jest.mock, and assert they were called
Client component that takes an action as a prop: pass vi.fn() as the action, so the form is tested without the server

chapters.title: Playwright End-to-End Testing
points: Setup: npm init playwright@latest; playwright.config.ts sets testDir, use.baseURL and webServer {command: 'npm run build && npm run start', url, reuseExistingServer: !process.env.CI}
Test E2E against the production build (next build && next start), not next dev, to catch real caching and rendering behavior
Locators auto-wait: page.getByRole('link', {name: 'Docs'}).click(); assert with await expect(page).toHaveURL(/docs/) and expect(locator).toBeVisible()
Commands: npx playwright test, --ui (interactive), --headed, --debug, --project=chromium, npx playwright show-report
Mistakes: hard-coded waitForTimeout, CSS/XPath selectors instead of role/test-id, tests that share state or depend on order

chapters.title: instrumentation.ts, Error Boundaries and Reporting
points: instrumentation.ts at project root (or src/) exports register(), which runs once per server instance at startup; use it to init OpenTelemetry or an error SDK
Guard runtime-specific code: if (process.env.NEXT_RUNTIME === 'nodejs') { await import('./instrumentation-node') } to avoid Edge bundling errors
Export onRequestError(err, request, context) to report all server errors (render, route handler, action, middleware) to Sentry or similar with route and request info
error.tsx must be a Client Component ('use client') receiving {error, reset}; it catches errors in its segment's children, not in the same-level layout; call reset() to retry
global-error.tsx replaces the root layout and must render its own <html> and <body>; in production, server errors reach the client with a generic message and error.digest to match against server logs
Event handlers and async code are not caught by boundaries, so use try/catch there; expected errors should be returned from Server Actions as values (useActionState), not thrown

chapters.title: Web Vitals and Testing Cheat Sheet
points: Core Web Vitals thresholds (good): LCP under 2.5s, INP under 200ms, CLS under 0.1; other metrics are FCP and TTFB
Report them with useReportWebVitals from 'next/web-vitals' inside a 'use client' component placed in the root layout, then POST via navigator.sendBeacon to your analytics
Lab vs field: Lighthouse is lab data; real-user field data (CrUX, your own reporting) is what counts
Cheat sheet commands: vitest run | jest | npx playwright test --ui | npx playwright show-report | npx next build && npx next start
Cheat sheet rules: units via RTL, async Server Components via E2E, Playwright on prod build, register() for init, onRequestError for reporting, error.tsx is client-only, global-error needs html/body
